# Microsoft Azure Bot classic deployment model client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Bot Service provides an integrated development environment for bot building. Its integration with Power Virtual Agents, a fully hosted low-code platform, enables developers of all technical abilities build conversational AI bots—no code needed.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Bot Service resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Bot Service management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.BotService
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Hidden obsolete factory retains the Omnichannel model
proposals.explanation: The obsolete editor-hidden Omnichannel factory passes default channelName and additional data plus ETag, provisioning state and location to the internal constructor; its message names Dynamics365OmnichannelChannel as the replacement.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The concrete obsolete factory body is under src/Customization outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Suppressed string reads replaced by typed channel-name operations
proposals.explanation: Get and GetAsync take BotChannelName, convert it with ToString for a scope-bound REST request, deserialize BotChannelData and construct BotChannelResource. A null model raises RequestFailedException; diagnostic failures are recorded and rethrown.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSuppress targets the string signatures and complete replacements are supplied outside Generated in src/Customization.

proposals.subtype: Typed channel existence reads explicitly branch on HTTP status
proposals.explanation: Exists and ExistsAsync convert BotChannelName to a request string, send a GET, deserialize only status 200, use a null model for 404, throw RequestFailedException for other statuses and return whether the resulting model is nonnull.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit signature suppressions and full typed replacements are captured under src/Customization outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Typed optional channel reads return a no-value response
proposals.explanation: GetIfExists and its async counterpart send a BotChannelName-derived GET, deserialize status 200, use a null model for 404 and reject other statuses. A null model becomes NoValueResponse; otherwise the body constructs BotChannelResource.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSuppress plus the complete replacements establishes handwritten customization beyond merely generated status-handling boilerplate.

proposals.subtype: Handwritten channel-data partial declares a tracked resource base
proposals.explanation: BotChannelData explicitly declares TrackedResourceData in the customization partial, alongside a comment identifying inheritance compatibility as its purpose; the generated companion is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The substantive base-type declaration and explicit inheritance-customization comment are under src/Customization outside Generated, despite the empty body.

proposals.explanation: The handwritten BotConnectionSettingData partial declares TrackedResourceData and labels that declaration as a compatibility customization; no generated-hierarchy comparison is asserted.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured non-generated Customization file explicitly declares the intended base rather than an unqualified empty partial.

proposals.explanation: The Customization partial declares BotData : TrackedResourceData with a comment identifying its intended compatibility role; the current generated output is not independently available.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: A substantive inheritance declaration plus an explicit customization-purpose comment is supplied outside Generated.

proposals.explanation: BotServicePrivateLinkResourceData explicitly declares ResourceData in the handwritten partial and identifies inheritance compatibility as its purpose, without a supplied generated counterpart.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The explicit resource base declaration and compatibility comment are in non-generated src/Customization source.

proposals.subtype: String identifier factory suppressed in favor of BotChannelName
proposals.explanation: CodeGenSuppress targets the four-string CreateResourceIdentifier signature; the replacement takes BotChannelName and interpolates it into the botServices/channels ARM path before constructing ResourceIdentifier.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: An explicit suppression and implemented replacement factory are captured under src/Customization outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Bot channel reads preserve the typed channel-name surface
proposals.explanation: The string GetBotChannel signatures are suppressed and the BotChannelName sync/async replacements call GetBotChannels().Get/GetAsync with the typed argument and cancellation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The generator annotations and actual typed forwarding bodies are captured in the non-generated Customization partial.

proposals.subtype: Regenerate-keys helper selects a channel and delegates its action
proposals.explanation: The sync/async helpers reject null content, select WebChatChannel only for the corresponding enum value and DirectLineChannel otherwise, construct a channel resource identifier from the bot's stored scope and selected name, get the resource through Client and forward the regenerate-keys action.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The selection and resource-binding bodies are explicitly implemented under src/Customization outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete polymorphic model retains a discriminator constructor
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete Omnichannel class derives from BotChannelProperties; its public constructor passes Omnichannel as the discriminator and its internal constructor forwards all supplied base-model state.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The actual legacy model definition and substantive base-constructor arguments are supplied outside Generated under src/Customization.

proposals.subtype: Legacy channel JSON reader handles typed fields and additional raw values
proposals.explanation: The reader returns null for JSON null, defaults channelName to Omnichannel, reads channelName/etag/provisioningState/location, skips null ETag/location values and retains unrecognized property raw JSON only when options.Format is not W. JSON and BinaryData creation paths enforce J format, mapping W through GetFormatFromOptions, and call this reader.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The property-by-property deserializer and explicit creation entry points are captured in Customization source outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Legacy channel write interfaces enforce JSON and delegate base fields
proposals.explanation: PersistableModelWriteCore accepts J after mapping W and uses ModelReaderWriter with the BotService serialization context; unsupported formats throw FormatException. IJsonModel.Write writes object delimiters and JsonModelWriteCore validates J then delegates field writing to the base implementation. GetFormatFromOptions returns J.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Actual interface and override bodies are supplied outside Generated in the Customization serialization partial.

proposals.explanation: The public RegenerateKeysBotChannelName enum declares WebChatChannel = 0 and DirectLineChannel = 1; it is an ordinary integer enum, not a string-backed or extensible enum.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete enum is supplied under src/Customization outside Generated with an explicit retained-API customization comment.

The typed replacements are supported, but legacy-overload-compatibility describes retained forwarding overloads, whereas the string members are suppressed and these methods implement the requests themselves. The revised pattern names the typed path-parameter replacement.

decisions.reason: Both handwritten methods validate content, choose a channel name from the enum, bind the bot's stored scope into a channel resource identifier and invoke its regenerate-keys method. The bound-resource-operation-overload pattern captures this reusable forwarding shape; the particular enum mapping is service-specific.

The obsolete, editor-hidden public Omnichannel class and its discriminator and state-forwarding constructors are implemented outside Generated. The compatibility-shim pattern is appropriate; the class itself is distinct from its factory and serialization methods.

The handwritten deserializer reads the cited model fields and preserves unknown raw JSON conditionally, while the cited creation entry points enforce the supported format and call it. This supports a custom model JSON reader, not an inference about other models.

The separate handwritten write path maps W to J, rejects unsupported formats, uses the serialization context, and implements the JSON write/interface bridge while delegating base-field writing. The cited lines support the distinct write-facing behavior, though no replacement of base field encoding is claimed.

The retained two-value integer enum is captured, but backward-compatibility-shim is too broad as a reusable pattern. The revised pattern specifically describes keeping a previously generated enum in handwritten source; generator capability is plausible, not confirmed.
